These estimates assume strong credit (700+), first-time Aston Martin buyer status, and Miami-area dealer pricing. Existing Aston Martin clients with purchase history can often negotiate better money factors — sometimes significantly so.

Why Lease an Aston Martin in Miami?

Leasing makes particular sense for Aston Martins, and Miami amplifies the advantages:

Florida Tax Benefits

  • No state income tax: More disposable income for that monthly payment.
  • Sales tax on lease payments only: In Florida, you pay sales tax on the monthly payment, not the full vehicle price. On a $250K DB12, this saves you $10,000–12,000 compared to states that tax the full amount at purchase.

Depreciation Protection

Aston Martins historically depreciate faster than their Italian and German competitors. A new DB12 can lose 35–45% of its value in three years. Leasing shifts that depreciation risk to the finance company. When the lease ends, you hand back the keys and move on — or into the next model.

Always Drive Current

Aston Martin is in the middle of a product renaissance. The new Vantage, DB12, and upcoming Vanquish represent a generational leap in performance and technology. A 36-month lease keeps you in the latest model without the long-term commitment.

Year-Round Enjoyment

Unlike leasing an Aston in Boston or Chicago, where it sits garaged half the year, Miami's climate means you're driving it 365 days. Your cost per drive drops dramatically.

Where to Lease an Aston Martin in Miami

Aston Martin Miami — The Authorized Dealer

Aston Martin Miami (formerly The Collection's Aston Martin division) is the city's authorized dealer, located at 200 Bird Road in Coral Gables alongside The Collection's Ferrari, Maserati, and Alfa Romeo showrooms. They handle Aston Martin Financial Services leasing directly and typically stock 20–35 new and pre-owned Aston Martins.

Why go here: Factory-backed lease rates, access to limited allocations, Aston Martin Timeless (CPO) program, and a service center with factory-trained technicians. They also offer track day experiences at Homestead-Miami Speedway for new clients — a serious perk.

Third-Party Exotic Leasing

Companies like Premier Financial Services and Putnam Leasing specialize in exotic car leases and can sometimes offer more flexible terms than the factory program — especially on pre-owned Aston Martins. They're worth getting a competitive quote from, particularly if you're leasing a pre-owned model that isn't eligible for AMFS rates.

Best Aston Martin Models to Lease in Miami

Vantage — Best Value Lease

The 2025+ Vantage is the entry point to Aston Martin ownership, but calling it "entry-level" undersells it completely. The Mercedes-AMG-sourced 4.0L twin-turbo V8 now produces 656 horsepower — making it the most powerful Vantage ever. It's compact, aggressive, and sounds phenomenal with the exhaust in Sport+ mode echoing off Brickell's towers.

At under $2,000/month with money down, it's the most accessible Aston Martin lease and arguably the best-looking sports car in its price range.

DB12 — Best All-Rounder

The DB12 replaced the DB11 and earned the title of the world's first "Super Tourer." It's the car you take on a weekend drive to Naples, park at the valet at Nobu, and still enjoy on a Tuesday commute. With 671 horsepower from the twin-turbo V8, gorgeous proportions, and a cabin that rivals anything from Bentley, the DB12 is the quintessential Miami grand tourer.

For convertible lovers, the DB12 Volante is the ultimate Miami Aston — top down, crossing the Rickenbacker Causeway at sunset. If you're going to lease one car that defines the Miami lifestyle, this might be it.

DBX707 — Best Daily Driver

The DBX707 is the world's most powerful luxury SUV — 707 horsepower in a vehicle that can handle school runs, airport pickups, and weekend getaways. It's Aston Martin's answer to the Lamborghini Urus, with more refinement and (arguably) better looks.

For Miami buyers who need practicality but refuse to sacrifice performance or style, the DBX707 lease is compelling. It handles Miami's speed bumps and parking garages without drama while still turning heads at every stoplight.

Aston Martin Lease Tips for Miami Buyers

1. Negotiate the Money Factor

The money factor (essentially the interest rate) on an Aston Martin lease is negotiable, especially if you have strong credit and are willing to put more money down. Even a small reduction in money factor can save $100–200/month on a $250K vehicle.

2. Watch Your Miles

Standard Aston Martin leases include 7,500–10,000 miles per year. Miami's compact geography helps here — most destinations are within 20 miles. But if you plan weekend trips to Key West, Naples, or Orlando, negotiate for 12,000 miles/year upfront. Overage fees are typically $0.50–$1.00 per mile.

3. Get Insurance Quotes First

Aston Martin insurance in Miami-Dade County runs $4,000–$10,000 annually depending on the model and your profile. The DBX707 is surprisingly affordable to insure compared to the sports cars. Get quotes from Hagerty, Chubb, and AIG Private Client before signing — they consistently beat standard carriers for exotic vehicles.

4. Consider Aston Martin Timeless (CPO)

Aston Martin's certified pre-owned program, called "Timeless," covers cars up to 10 years old with a factory-backed warranty. Leasing a Timeless DB11 or previous-gen Vantage can save $500–800/month versus leasing new, with minimal compromise on the driving experience.

5. Explore Business Lease Options

If you're a business owner — and this is Miami, so statistically you might be — consult your CPA about deducting lease payments. The Section 179 deduction and bonus depreciation rules can make a meaningful dent in the effective cost of a DBX707 lease in particular, given its weight qualifies for enhanced deductions.

Aston Martin Lease vs. Buy: The Math

For most Aston Martin models, leasing wins the financial argument:

  • Depreciation: Aston Martins lose 35–45% in three years. On a $250K DB12, that's $87,000–$112,000 in depreciation. A lease caps your exposure.
  • Warranty alignment: The factory warranty covers the full lease term, so you're never out of pocket for surprise repairs.
  • Model freshness: With Aston Martin releasing significant updates every 2–3 years, leasing keeps you current.

The exception: if Aston Martin releases a limited-production model and you get an allocation (like the Valour or upcoming Valhalla), buying makes more sense — limited models tend to hold value or appreciate.

Aston Martin in Miami: More Than a Car

Aston Martin Miami doesn't just sell cars — they offer a lifestyle ecosystem. Owners get access to:

  • Art of Living experiences: Private events, motorsport experiences, and curated lifestyle events throughout South Florida
  • Aston Martin Residences: Miami's 66-story Aston Martin-branded luxury tower in Downtown, with a unique tie-in for car owners
  • Track events: Regular track days at Homestead-Miami Speedway exclusively for Aston Martin owners

The Aston Martin Residences at 300 Biscayne Boulevard Way are particularly noteworthy — it's one of the few places where you can live in your car brand. Penthouse buyers even receive an Aston Martin Vulcan as part of the purchase. The building's car elevator and private garage suites are designed specifically for Aston Martin ownership.

Bottom Line on Aston Martin Leasing in Miami

An Aston Martin lease in Miami starts at roughly $1,800/month for a Vantage — less than renting one for a single weekend. With Florida's tax advantages, year-round driving weather, and one of the best authorized dealer experiences in the country, Miami is arguably the best city in America to lease an Aston Martin.

Start at Aston Martin Miami in Coral Gables, test drive the DB12 Volante across the causeway, and see if you can hand back the keys. We bet you can't.

title: DuPont Registry Miami: How to Buy & Sell Luxury Cars in 2026
excerpt: DuPont Registry has been the go-to marketplace for high-end vehicles since 1985. Here's how Miami buyers and sellers use it to move exotic and luxury cars — and what alternatives exist.
content:
If you've ever shopped for a six-figure car in South Florida, you've encountered DuPont Registry. Founded in 1985 in Tampa, DuPont Registry started as a glossy print magazine that became the bible of luxury car buying — the kind of publication you'd find in the waiting rooms of private aviation terminals and Porsche dealerships. Today, DuPont Registry operates as a digital marketplace at dupontregistry.com, and it remains one of the most recognized names in high-end automotive sales.

For Miami buyers and sellers, DuPont Registry occupies a unique position: it's where serious money meets serious metal. Here's everything you need to know about using DuPont Registry in Miami in 2026 — whether you're buying your first exotic or listing a seven-figure collection car.

What Is DuPont Registry?

DuPont Registry is a luxury marketplace specializing in high-end vehicles, real estate, and yachts. The automotive side — which is what most people know it for — features listings from both dealers and private sellers across the United States, with a heavy concentration in Florida, California, and Texas.

The platform focuses exclusively on premium vehicles. You won't find a 2019 Camry here. The typical DuPont Registry listing features Ferraris, Lamborghinis, Rolls-Royces, Bentleys, classic Porsches, vintage muscle, and the occasional hypercar that costs more than most Miami condos. The average listing price sits well into six figures, and seven-figure cars appear regularly.

DuPont Registry vs. Other Luxury Car Marketplaces

Miami buyers have several options for finding exotic and luxury vehicles. Here's how DuPont Registry stacks up:

PlatformFocusListing CostBest ForMiami Presence
DuPont RegistryLuxury & exotic$99–$495/listing (private); dealer packages availableHigh-end new & used exoticsVery strong
Bring a TrailerAuction formatFree to list; 5% buyer's feeEnthusiast cars, classics, unique findsStrong
Cars & BidsAuction formatFree to list; 4.5% buyer's feeModern enthusiast & sports carsModerate
AutoTraderAll vehiclesDealer-focusedVolume searching, mainstream + luxuryStrong
HemmingsClassics & muscle$30–$100/listingPre-1990 classics, muscle carsModerate
Exotic Car TraderExotics onlyDealer packagesNewer exotic inventoryStrong

DuPont Registry's advantage is brand recognition and buyer quality. Listings on DuPont attract qualified, high-net-worth buyers who know what they're looking for — not tire-kickers sending lowball offers. For sellers of $200K+ vehicles, that audience quality matters more than raw traffic numbers.

How to Buy a Car Through DuPont Registry in Miami

Buying through DuPont Registry is straightforward, but the stakes are higher than a typical car purchase. Here's the process:

Step 1: Search and Filter

Visit dupontregistry.com and use the search filters to narrow by make, model, year, price range, and location. Filter by Florida or Miami specifically to find local inventory — this matters because inspecting a car in person is non-negotiable at these price points.

Step 2: Verify the Seller

DuPont Registry lists both dealers and private sellers. Dealer listings from established Miami businesses like The Collection, Prestige Imports, South Beach Exotic Rentals' sales division, and Curated are generally safer — they have reputations to protect. Private sellers require more due diligence.

Step 3: Pre-Purchase Inspection (PPI)

Never skip a pre-purchase inspection on an exotic car, regardless of the seller's reputation. In Miami, several shops specialize in PPI for high-end vehicles:

  • The Barn Miami — Known for thorough Ferrari and Lamborghini inspections
  • Prestige European Auto in Coral Gables — Covers Porsche, Aston Martin, Bentley
  • Foreign Affairs Motorsport in Pompano Beach — One of the largest independent exotic service centers in Florida

A PPI typically costs $300–$800 for an exotic car and can save you tens of thousands by uncovering hidden issues. Paint thickness readings, compression tests, and full electronic scans are standard at this level.

Step 4: Negotiate and Close

Pricing on DuPont Registry is typically listed as "Contact for Price" or at a stated asking price. Unlike auction platforms, there's room to negotiate. Miami's competitive dealer landscape means you have leverage — there are more exotic cars for sale per capita in South Florida than almost anywhere in the country.

How to Sell a Car on DuPont Registry From Miami

If you're selling a luxury or exotic car from Miami, DuPont Registry puts your listing in front of the right audience. Here's how to maximize your results:

Listing Options and Costs

Private sellers can list individual vehicles starting at $99 for a basic listing (photos + description) up to $495 for a premium featured listing with enhanced placement. Dealers typically purchase monthly or annual packages that include multiple listings and premium positioning.

Photography Matters — A Lot

DuPont Registry buyers expect professional-quality photos. Miami actually gives you an advantage here: the lighting is incredible. Shoot during golden hour (7:00–8:00 AM or 6:00–7:00 PM) in a clean location. The Miami Design District, Wynwood walls, and waterfront spots along Brickell all make stunning backdrops that scream Miami lifestyle.

If you're selling a $100K+ vehicle, invest $200–$500 in professional automotive photography. Several Miami photographers specialize in car shoots and know the best locations. It's the highest-ROI money you can spend on a listing.

Pricing Strategy

Research comparable sales on Bring a Trailer (completed auctions show actual transaction prices), check Hagerty's valuation tools for classics, and review current DuPont Registry listings for similar vehicles. Miami tends to command a slight premium for certain makes — convertibles, bright colors, and anything associated with Miami car culture sells faster and higher here than in most markets.

DuPont Registry's Miami Connection

Although DuPont Registry is headquartered in the Tampa Bay area, Miami has always been its spiritual home market. The magazine's covers frequently featured cars photographed against Miami backdrops — Ocean Drive, the Fontainebleau, Key Biscayne causeways. The intersection of wealth, car culture, and lifestyle that defines Miami is essentially DuPont Registry's brand identity.

Today, Miami-area dealers make up a significant portion of DuPont Registry's inventory. The city's role as a hub for Latin American wealth means buyers routinely purchase vehicles through DuPont for export to Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, and beyond — often through Florida's Foreign Trade Zone advantages.

Top Miami Dealers on DuPont Registry

These Miami-area dealers consistently list inventory on DuPont Registry and are worth checking directly:

  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — Ferrari, Aston Martin, Maserati, Alfa Romeo. One of the largest exotic dealerships in the Southeast.
  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Lamborghini, Pagani, Koenigsegg. Miami's Lamborghini authority.
  • Curated (Miami) — Boutique gallery-style dealership with rotating hyper-luxury inventory.
  • South Motors (various South Miami locations) — BMW, Porsche, and more. Strong pre-owned luxury selection.
  • Warren Henry Auto Group (North Miami) — Jaguar, Land Rover, Bugatti, Lamborghini, Koenigsegg.
  • Braman Motorcars (Palm Beach / Miami) — Bentley, Rolls-Royce, Porsche, BMW.

Alternatives to DuPont Registry for Miami Car Buyers

While DuPont Registry is excellent for traditional buy/sell transactions, Miami's market has expanded significantly:

Bring a Trailer (BaT)

The auction platform has become the go-to for enthusiast cars in the $50K–$500K range. Miami sellers love BaT because the competitive auction format often pushes prices above what a fixed listing would achieve. The 7-day auction creates urgency that benefits sellers.

Instagram and Social Selling

In Miami's car scene, Instagram is a legitimate sales channel. Dealers like Curated and consignment specialists regularly sell cars directly through Instagram stories and posts. Follow accounts like @cuaboratk, @rfrsh.miami, and @southbeachexotics for inventory that may never hit traditional platforms.

Car Shows and Events

Events like Supercar Saturdays Bal Harbour, Cars and Coffee Aventura, and the annual Festival of Speed at the Ritz-Carlton Amelia Island (a short drive north) are where deals happen face-to-face. Many of the best cars change hands through relationships built at these events, never hitting a public listing.

Tips for Miami Exotic Car Transactions

Whether you're using DuPont Registry or any other platform, keep these Miami-specific tips in mind:

  • Title transfer: Florida titles are handled through your local tax collector's office. For vehicles over $100K, use a title and registration service to avoid DMV lines and ensure everything is filed correctly.
  • Sales tax: Florida charges 6% state sales tax plus county surtax (1% in Miami-Dade) on vehicle purchases. Out-of-state buyers may owe tax in their home state instead — consult a tax professional.
  • Escrow for private sales: For transactions above $50K between private parties, use an escrow service. Companies like Escrow.com and Premium Trust specialize in vehicle transactions and protect both buyer and seller.
  • Hurricane history: Always run a Carfax and check for flood or hurricane damage — Florida's storm history means this is a real risk, especially on pre-owned vehicles that may have been through a storm zone.
  • Import considerations: If buying a vehicle for export, ensure compliance with the destination country's import regulations. Miami has multiple customs brokers specializing in vehicle exports to Latin America and the Caribbean.

The Bottom Line on DuPont Registry in Miami

DuPont Registry remains one of the best platforms for buying and selling luxury vehicles in Miami. Its audience is qualified, its brand carries weight with serious collectors and buyers, and its deep roots in the Florida luxury market make it a natural fit for the city's exotic car scene.

For buyers, it's a curated starting point that filters out the noise. For sellers, it's access to buyers who can actually write the check. In a city with more exotic cars per square mile than almost anywhere in America, that combination is worth the listing fee.

title: The Lamborghini Countach: Miami's Defining Supercar
excerpt: No car is more synonymous with 1980s Miami than the Lamborghini Countach. From Miami Vice to bedroom wall posters, here's how the Countach became Miami's defining supercar — and what it's worth today.
content:
If you could distill 1980s Miami into a single object, it would be a white Lamborghini Countach parked in front of a pastel Art Deco hotel on Ocean Drive. No car in automotive history is more tightly linked to a city and an era than the Countach is to Miami. It wasn't just a car — it was the visual shorthand for excess, ambition, and the electric energy that defined South Florida's most iconic decade.

Today, the Lamborghini Countach commands six- and seven-figure prices at auction, draws crowds at every Miami car show, and remains the poster car — literally — that introduced an entire generation to the idea that cars could be art. Here's the full story of Miami's defining supercar.

The Lamborghini Countach: A Brief History

The Countach story begins in 1971 at the Geneva Motor Show, where Lamborghini unveiled the LP 500 prototype designed by Marcello Gandini at Bertone. Legend has it that when Nuccio Bertone first saw the design, he exclaimed "countach!" — a Piedmontese exclamation roughly translating to an expression of astonishment. The name stuck.

Production began in 1974 with the LP400 and continued through five major variants over 16 years:

VariantYearsEnginePowerUnits Built
LP4001974–19783.9L V12370 hp157
LP400 S1978–19823.9L V12353 hp235
LP500 S1982–19854.8L V12370 hp321
5000 QV1985–19885.2L V12455 hp610
25th Anniversary1988–19905.2L V12455 hp657

Total production across all variants: approximately 1,980 units. For context, Lamborghini now sells that many Urus SUVs in about two months. The Countach was, and remains, genuinely rare.

Why the Countach Became Miami's Car

The Miami Vice Effect

When Miami Vice premiered on NBC in September 1984, it didn't just change television — it changed Miami's identity. The show's visual language — pastel suits, neon lights, art deco architecture, and exotic cars — defined an aesthetic that still influences Miami's culture 40 years later.

While Sonny Crockett's white Ferrari Testarossa got most of the screen time, the Lamborghini Countach appeared repeatedly throughout the series and became even more synonymous with the show's world of drug kingpins, nightclubs, and waterfront mansions. The Countach was the villain's car — the car that pulled up to the nightclub, the car parked in the marble-floored garage of the Coral Gables estate. It was aspirational in the most dangerous, intoxicating way.

The Poster That Changed Everything

Before the internet, before Instagram, car culture spread through posters. And no automotive poster was more ubiquitous in the 1980s than the Lamborghini Countach — typically a black or white LP500 S, shot from a low angle, parked in front of a palm-lined driveway or a Miami mansion.

That poster hung in millions of bedrooms around the world. For an entire generation, the Countach was the first supercar they ever saw. It shaped their idea of what "cool" looked like — and cool looked like Miami.

Miami's Wealth Boom

The 1980s were Miami's coming-of-age party. The cocaine trade, for all its devastating social impact, poured unprecedented cash into the city. Real estate boomed. Nightlife exploded. And the newly wealthy — both legitimate and otherwise — needed cars that matched the lifestyle. The Countach, with its outrageous design and astronomical price tag (around $100,000 in 1985 dollars, equivalent to roughly $280,000 today), was the ultimate status symbol.

Miami became one of the largest markets for Lamborghini in North America. The cars weren't just transportation — they were declarations. In a city where subtlety was suspicious, the Countach's wing, scoops, and angles said everything that needed to be said.

Lamborghini Countach Design: Why It Still Stops Traffic

Marcello Gandini's design for the Countach broke every rule of automotive design — and created new ones that designers still reference today. The key elements:

  • The wedge shape: Nearly flat from nose to windshield, the Countach pioneered the wedge profile that defined supercars for decades. Every Lamborghini since — the Diablo, Murciélago, Aventador, and Revuelto — traces its silhouette back to the Countach.
  • Scissor doors: The Countach didn't invent upward-opening doors, but it made them iconic. The doors rotate forward and up on a hinge near the A-pillar. Lamborghini has used scissor doors on every flagship since, and they remain the brand's most recognizable design element.
  • The rear wing: The massive rear spoiler on later Countach models (LP500 S onward) became one of the most imitated design elements in automotive history. It was functional — somewhat — but mostly it was theater. And it worked.
  • NACA ducts and scoops: The Countach's body is covered in functional air intakes that feed the mid-mounted V12. The massive side scoops on the 5000 QV give the car its most aggressive profile and became a design language that screams "Lamborghini" to this day.

The genius of Gandini's design is that it still looks futuristic. Park a Countach on Ocean Drive today — next to new Ferraris, McLarens, and even the latest Lamborghini Revuelto — and the Countach still draws the biggest crowd. It transcended its era.

Driving a Lamborghini Countach in Miami

The Countach was designed to look like the future. Driving it feels more like wrestling a beautiful, angry animal. Here's what the experience is actually like:

The V12 Sound

The naturally aspirated V12 mounted longitudinally behind your head produces a mechanical symphony that no modern turbo engine can replicate. It's raw, loud, and intoxicating — especially in the canyons between Brickell's towers, where the sound bounces off glass and concrete. In a city full of loud cars, the Countach's V12 still turns heads.

The Visibility Challenge

Rearward visibility in a Countach is essentially zero. The rear window is a mail slot. The side mirrors are decorative at best. Backing up requires opening the door and looking behind you — which, in the Countach, means standing up on the sill because the car is so low you can't see past the engine cover. Miami traffic, with its aggressive lane-changers and motorcycles splitting between cars on I-95, makes this genuinely nerve-wracking.

No Air Conditioning (Effectively)

While later Countach models technically had air conditioning, the system is laughably inadequate by modern standards. The V12 generates so much heat that the cabin becomes an oven — doubly so in Miami's summer. Original owners in Miami often drove their Countachs only at night or during the cooler months. This remains true today: you'll see Countachs at Miami car shows almost exclusively during the October–April "season."

The Clutch

The Countach uses a gated manual transmission with a heavy, unassisted clutch. Stop-and-go traffic on the MacArthur Causeway will give your left leg a serious workout. There's no hill start assist, no creep mode, no forgiveness. You either drive it properly or you stall it in the intersection of Collins and 41st — and everyone will see.

Lamborghini Countach Values in 2026

The Countach market has appreciated dramatically over the past decade, driven by nostalgia, scarcity, and the growing collector car market. Here's where values stand:

VariantCondition2026 Value RangeTrend
LP400 (Periscopio)Excellent$1,500,000 – $2,500,000+📈 Strong appreciation
LP400 SExcellent$600,000 – $1,000,000📈 Rising steadily
LP500 SExcellent$500,000 – $800,000📈 Rising
5000 QVExcellent$450,000 – $750,000→ Stable to rising
25th AnniversaryExcellent$400,000 – $650,000→ Stable

The early LP400 "Periscopio" models (named for their periscope-style rearview mirror) are the most valuable, routinely crossing $2 million at auction. These were the purest expression of Gandini's design — no wing, clean lines, and only 157 built. They're the Countach that collectors covet most.

For buyers entering the Countach market, the 5000 QV and 25th Anniversary editions offer the best value: they're the most powerful, the most livable (relatively speaking), and the most numerous — making finding good examples slightly easier. "Slightly" being the operative word when you're shopping for a car with under 2,000 total production.

Where to See a Lamborghini Countach in Miami

Countachs appear regularly at Miami's premier car events:

  • Supercar Saturdays Bal Harbour: The monthly show at Bal Harbour Shops regularly draws Countach owners. The October–March season is prime Countach time.
  • Cars and Coffee Aventura: The casual Saturday morning meet occasionally features Countachs, especially during Art Basel week when collectors fly in their cars.
  • Festivals of Speed: The Ritz-Carlton shows (both Amelia Island and local events) feature curated Countach displays.
  • Prestige Imports: Miami's Lamborghini dealer occasionally displays classic Lamborghinis in their showroom alongside new Revueltos and Urus models.
  • Private collections: Miami is home to several world-class car collections. While most are private, events like the Concours d'Elegance at the Biltmore Hotel provide access to otherwise hidden Countachs.

The 2022 Countach LPI 800-4: Lamborghini's Modern Tribute

In 2021, Lamborghini unveiled the Countach LPI 800-4 — a limited-production hybrid supercar that paid homage to the original. Built on the Aventador's platform with a 6.5L V12 and a supercapacitor hybrid system producing 803 horsepower, the LPI 800-4 borrowed design cues from the original: the angular bodywork, the side strakes, and the rectangular taillights.

Only 112 units were produced, priced at approximately $2.6 million each — and all were sold before the public announcement. Several have been spotted in Miami, typically in white (a nod to the iconic 1980s Miami Countach spec). On the secondary market, they're already trading above $3 million.

Whether the modern Countach captures the original's magic is debatable — it's faster, safer, and infinitely more comfortable, but it lacks the raw mechanical drama that made the original a legend. In Miami, both versions draw crowds, but the original still commands the deeper emotional response.

Buying a Lamborghini Countach in Miami

If you're in the market for a Lamborghini Countach, Miami is one of the best places to shop. The city's concentration of exotic car dealers, consignment specialists, and private collectors means examples surface regularly:

  • DuPont Registry: The luxury marketplace frequently lists Countachs from Florida sellers. Search "Lamborghini Countach" and filter by Florida.
  • Bring a Trailer: Multiple Countachs sell on BaT annually. The platform's transparent auction format makes it easy to track market values.
  • Curated Miami: The boutique exotic dealer occasionally consigns Countachs and has the expertise to authenticate and value them properly.
  • RM Sotheby's / Gooding & Company: The major auction houses hold events in Amelia Island (March) and occasionally Miami, featuring top-tier Countach examples.

What to Inspect

Countach buyers should look for:

  • Originality: Matching-numbers engines, original body panels, and factory color combinations command significant premiums. A repainted or re-engined Countach can be worth 30–50% less than an original-spec car.
  • Service history: The V12 requires regular and expensive maintenance. A well-documented service history from qualified shops is essential.
  • Body condition: The Countach's aluminum and fiberglass body panels are hand-fitted. Panel gaps, paint quality, and structural integrity vary significantly between examples.
  • Florida history: Cars that have lived their lives in Florida benefit from no salt exposure (no road salt) but may show UV damage to paint, rubber, and interior materials if not properly stored.

The Countach Legacy in Miami

The Lamborghini Countach didn't just define a car era — it defined Miami's identity as a car city. The Countach proved that Miami wasn't just a beach town — it was a place where the world's most extreme machines belonged. It set the template for every supercar that has called Miami home since: be loud, be bold, be unapologetic.

Forty years after the Countach first rolled down Ocean Drive, Miami's car scene is bigger, louder, and more diverse than ever. Bugattis, Paganis, and Koenigseggs now share the streets with Teslas, G-Wagons, and custom-wrapped Lamborghini Urus SUVs. But the Countach started it all. It's the car that made Miami a supercar city — and every exotic that parks on South Beach today owes something to that wedge-shaped, scissor-doored, V12-screaming legend from Sant'Agata Bolognese.

If you've never seen one in person, make it a point to attend the next Supercar Saturdays at Bal Harbour or a concours event at the Biltmore. Stand next to a Countach. Take in the angles, the proportions, the sheer audacity of the design. Then try to imagine Miami without it. You can't. And that's exactly the point.

title: Best Pressure Washers for Car Detailing: A Miami Exotic Owner's Guide
excerpt: A quality pressure washer is the foundation of proper car care — especially in Miami, where salt air, road grime, and insect residue attack your paint daily. Here are the best pressure washers for detailing exotic cars at home.
content:
If you're serious about maintaining an exotic car in Miami, a pressure washer isn't a luxury — it's the foundation of your entire detailing routine. Hand-washing with a hose and bucket is fine for a Camry, but when you're dealing with $200K+ paint, ceramic coatings, and intricate aero surfaces full of brake dust, you need controlled, consistent water pressure that won't damage delicate finishes while still blasting away South Florida's uniquely aggressive contaminants.

We've evaluated the top pressure washers for car detailing in 2026 with a focus on what matters to Miami exotic owners: adjustable pressure for sensitive paint, foam cannon compatibility, portability, and the ability to handle the salt, sand, and bug residue that define South Florida driving.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need a Dedicated Pressure Washer

Automatic car washes are out of the question for any exotic — the brushes, recycled water, and harsh chemicals will destroy clear coat and ceramic coatings. Even touchless washes use chemicals that can strip wax and sealants. That leaves hand washing or a personal pressure washer setup. Here's why the pressure washer wins:

  • Pre-rinse decontamination: Miami's roads deposit a film of brake dust, salt residue, and insect remains that should be loosened before any contact washing. A pressure washer's pre-rinse step reduces the risk of scratching by removing 80% of surface contaminants before you ever touch the paint.
  • Foam cannon capability: Attach a foam cannon to your pressure washer and you get a thick blanket of cleaning foam that dwells on the surface, breaking down grime without scrubbing. It's the safest way to wash any car, and it's deeply satisfying to watch.
  • Underbody flushing: Miami's salt air corrodes undercarriage components. A pressure washer with an underbody attachment flushes salt deposits from chassis, suspension, and brake components — critical maintenance that a garden hose simply can't do.
  • Wheel cleaning: Exotic car brakes generate enormous amounts of brake dust (especially carbon ceramics). A pressure washer makes quick work of embedded dust in intricate wheel designs that would take 30+ minutes to clean by hand.

Best Pressure Washers for Car Detailing in 2026

1. Kranzle K 1622 TS — Best Overall for Exotic Cars

Price: ~$450–550 | PSI: 1,600 | GPM: 1.6 | Type: Electric

The Kranzle K 1622 TS is the pressure washer that professional detailers use on Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and Rolls-Royces — and for good reason. Built in Germany with an industrial-grade brass pump and sealed motor, this machine is engineered to run for thousands of hours. Many detailing shops report 10+ years of daily use from a single unit.

At 1,600 PSI and 1.6 GPM, it delivers the perfect pressure for automotive work — strong enough to blast away brake dust and road grime, gentle enough to use on ceramic-coated paint without risk. The Total Stop System (TS) automatically shuts off the pump when the trigger is released, extending pump life and reducing noise.

Why it's #1 for Miami: The brass pump handles Florida's hard water without the mineral buildup that kills cheaper aluminum pumps. It's also compact enough to store in a condo parking garage or small garage.

Best for: Serious enthusiasts and anyone who wants a "buy it for life" pressure washer.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Active VE52 Electric Pressure Washer — Best Value for Home Detailing

Price: ~$200–250 | PSI: 1,800 | GPM: 2.0 | Type: Electric

The Active VE52 has quietly become one of the most popular pressure washers in the detailing community. It delivers 1,800 PSI and 2.0 GPM — more flow than the Kranzle at less than half the price. The induction motor is whisper-quiet (important if you're washing in a condo complex at 7 AM), and the pump is built with brass internals.

It includes a foam cannon adapter, 25-foot hose, and a set of quick-connect nozzles. Out of the box, it's ready for detailing work with minimal additional purchases.

Why it works for Miami: The high GPM means faster rinsing — important when you're washing in the Miami heat and need to prevent water from drying on the paint before you can rinse. Quiet operation is a plus for residential areas.

Best for: Home detailers who want excellent performance without the Kranzle price tag.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. Greenworks 2000 PSI Electric Pressure Washer — Best Budget Option

Price: ~$150–180 | PSI: 2,000 | GPM: 1.2 | Type: Electric

If you're getting into pressure washer detailing and don't want to commit $500+, the Greenworks 2000 PSI is the entry point that detailing forums consistently recommend. It's lightweight (under 40 lbs), has a brushless motor, and comes with a foam cannon and multiple nozzle tips.

The trade-off versus pricier options is the lower GPM (1.2 vs 1.6–2.0), which means slower rinse times and slightly less effective foam action. But for most weekend warriors washing one or two cars, it gets the job done well.

Why it works for Miami: Compact and lightweight — perfect for apartment/condo dwellers who need to roll it out from storage. Works well on standard 120V outlets.

Best for: Budget-conscious enthusiasts washing 1-2 cars regularly.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. RYOBI 2300 PSI Brushless Electric Pressure Washer — Best for Versatility

Price: ~$250–300 | PSI: 2,300 | GPM: 1.2 | Type: Electric

The RYOBI 2300 PSI is the Swiss Army knife option. With adjustable pressure from 600 to 2,300 PSI via a dial on the wand, you can switch from a gentle rinse on your Ferrari's paint to full power on your driveway concrete in seconds. The brushless motor is efficient and long-lasting.

This versatility makes it ideal if you want one machine for car detailing AND household tasks — cleaning the garage floor, power-washing the patio after a Miami thunderstorm, or hosing down the boat.

Why it works for Miami: The adjustable PSI dial means you can dial down to 600 PSI for exotic paint and crank up to 2,300 PSI for cleaning salt deposits off driveway concrete. One tool, many jobs.

5. MJJC Foam Cannon Pro V2.0 + Any Pressure Washer — Best Foam Cannon Add-On

Price: ~$35–45 (foam cannon only) | Compatibility: Fits most electric/gas pressure washers

If you already own a pressure washer but want to upgrade your foam game, the MJJC Foam Cannon Pro V2.0 is the gold standard aftermarket foam cannon. It produces thicker, more consistent foam than the foam cannons bundled with most pressure washers, and it's adjustable from thin rinse foam to thick "snow foam" that clings to vertical panels for minutes.

The V2.0 version includes improved seals, a metal connector (instead of plastic), and an adjustable fan pattern. Pair it with a quality snow foam soap like Chemical Guys Honeydew Snow Foam for the safest possible touchless pre-wash.

Best for: Anyone upgrading an existing pressure washer setup for better foam performance.

Electric vs. Gas: Why Electric Wins for Car Detailing

Gas pressure washers deliver more PSI (3,000+), but for car detailing they're actually worse:

  • Too much pressure: 3,000+ PSI can strip paint, damage trim, and push water past seals. You'd need to stand much farther back, reducing cleaning effectiveness and foam cannon performance.
  • No auto-stop: Gas units run continuously. Electric units with auto-stop (like the Kranzle TS) shut off when you release the trigger — saving wear, reducing noise, and preventing overheating.
  • Noise: Gas pressure washers are loud enough to anger every neighbor in your building. Electric models are quiet enough to use at dawn in a Miami condo complex without complaints.
  • Exhaust: Can't run a gas pressure washer inside a garage. Electric runs anywhere you have an outlet.

For home car detailing in Miami, electric is the clear choice. Save gas pressure washers for driveway and construction work.

Essential Pressure Washer Accessories for Car Detailing

A pressure washer alone isn't a complete detailing setup. Here's what to add:

Foam Cannon

If your pressure washer didn't come with one, the MJJC Foam Cannon Pro V2.0 (~$35) is the upgrade to make. Thick foam = safer washing.

Microfiber Wash Mitt

After the foam cannon pre-wash, use a plush microfiber wash mitt (not a sponge) for contact washing. The Rag Company Cyclone Wash Mitt (~$15) is the detailing community's favorite.

Filtered Water System

Miami's tap water is hard — loaded with minerals that leave water spots on dark paint. A deionized water filter like the CR Spotless Water De-Ionizing System (~$300–400) attaches to your water line and produces spot-free rinse water. On a dark-colored exotic, this is transformative — you can let the car air dry without a single water spot.

Undercarriage Cleaner Attachment

For flushing salt air deposits from your underbody, an undercarriage cleaner attachment (~$20–30) rolls under the car and sprays upward. In Miami's coastal environment, this should be part of your monthly wash routine.

How to Safely Pressure Wash an Exotic Car

The Two-Bucket + Foam Cannon Method

  1. Pre-rinse: Use the pressure washer with a 40-degree (white) nozzle from 3+ feet away to rinse loose dirt, sand, and debris. Never use the 0-degree (red) nozzle on paint.
  2. Foam: Switch to the foam cannon with a quality pH-neutral car shampoo. Coat the entire car in thick foam and let it dwell for 3–5 minutes.
  3. Rinse foam: Rinse the foam off with the pressure washer. This step alone removes the majority of contaminants without touching the paint.
  4. Contact wash: Using the two-bucket method (one wash, one rinse), gently wash panels from top to bottom with a microfiber mitt.
  5. Final rinse: Rinse with filtered/DI water if available. Otherwise, rinse quickly and dry immediately with a quality drying towel to prevent water spots.
  6. Dry: Use a plush drying towel or a filtered air blower. In Miami's heat, you need to move fast — water evaporates quickly and leaves mineral deposits.

Miami-Specific Tips

  • Wash in shade: Never pressure wash in direct Miami sunlight. The water and soap will dry on the paint faster than you can rinse, leaving spots and streaks. Early morning (before 9 AM) or under a covered parking structure is ideal.
  • Bug removal: South Florida's love bugs (especially April–May and August–September) are acidic enough to etch paint if left for more than 48 hours. A dedicated bug remover spray before the foam cannon step makes quick work of them.
  • Weekly washes: In Miami's environment, washing every 7–10 days prevents salt and contaminant buildup from damaging paint and coatings. A pressure washer makes this a 30-minute task instead of a 90-minute ordeal.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the Active VE52 offers the best combination of performance, price, and quiet operation for home detailing. If you want the professional-grade tool that Miami's top detailers trust, the Kranzle K 1622 TS is the buy-it-once-cry-once option that will outlast your car collection. And if you're just getting started, the Greenworks 2000 PSI proves you don't need to spend $500 to properly wash an exotic.

Pair any of these with a quality foam cannon, filtered water, and a good microfiber mitt, and you've got a detailing setup that would make most professional shops jealous. Your Miami exotic's paint will thank you. 💦

title: Best GPS Trackers for Exotic Cars: Protect Your Miami Investment
excerpt: Miami ranks among the top US cities for exotic car theft and insurance fraud. A hidden GPS tracker is the best way to recover your investment if the worst happens. Here are the top GPS trackers for exotic car owners in 2026.
content:
Here's a number that should concern every exotic car owner in Miami: Florida ranks #1 in the US for vehicle theft, and Miami-Dade County is consistently among the state's worst counties. When your car is worth $200K to $2M+, it's not just a vehicle — it's a target. And while alarm systems and steering wheel locks deter opportunists, a GPS tracker is what actually gets your car back when a professional takes it.

We've evaluated the best GPS trackers for exotic cars based on what matters most: real-time accuracy, battery life, tamper resistance, covert installation, geofencing, and the kind of instant alerts that give law enforcement — and you — the edge in recovery situations.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need GPS Tracking

Miami's exotic car theft landscape is uniquely dangerous:

  • Port proximity: The Port of Miami and Port Everglades are two of the busiest shipping ports in the US. Stolen exotics can be loaded into a container and on a ship to South America, the Caribbean, or West Africa within hours of being taken. Once it's on a boat, it's gone. A GPS tracker is the only way to intercept before that happens.
  • Relay theft: Modern keyless-entry exotics (virtually all of them in 2026) are vulnerable to relay attacks, where thieves use signal amplifiers to trick the car into thinking the key fob is nearby. The car unlocks and starts without breaking a single thing. This has been documented on Ferraris, Lamborghinis, Porsches, and Range Rovers in Miami.
  • Valet risk: Miami's valet culture means your keys are regularly in someone else's hands. A GPS tracker with geofence alerts tells you immediately if your car leaves an authorized area — like the restaurant parking lot you're currently sitting in.
  • Insurance requirements: Some high-value vehicle insurers (Chubb, AIG, Hagerty) offer premium discounts for vehicles with active GPS tracking systems. On a $10,000+/year exotic car policy, that discount can effectively pay for the tracker.

Best GPS Trackers for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. LandAirSea Overdrive — Best Overall for Exotic Cars

Price: ~$30 device + $20–25/month service | Battery: Up to 1 year (magnet mount) | Update Rate: Real-time (3-second intervals)

The LandAirSea Overdrive is the tracker that private investigators, fleet managers, and car enthusiasts trust most. It's remarkably small (about the size of a deck of cards), waterproof, and has a built-in magnet mount strong enough to hold onto any metal surface under your car at highway speeds.

What makes it ideal for exotic cars:

  • Real-time tracking: 3-second location updates mean law enforcement can track your car block by block. No 30-second or 1-minute delays that let thieves disappear.
  • Geofencing: Set virtual boundaries around your home, office, or favorite restaurants. Get an instant push notification if your car crosses the boundary — invaluable for valet monitoring.
  • Speed alerts: Set speed thresholds and get alerts if someone is driving your car faster than allowed. Useful for valet monitoring and if a family member borrows the car.
  • 1-year battery: In the extended-life magnetic mount, the Overdrive runs for up to a year on a single charge. No hardwiring required, meaning zero risk of electrical issues in your exotic's sensitive systems.

Best for: Most exotic owners. The combination of price, battery life, and real-time accuracy is unmatched.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Bouncie Smart Driving Companion — Best OBD-II Plug-In Tracker

Price: ~$80 device + $8/month service | Battery: Vehicle-powered (OBD-II) | Update Rate: Real-time (15-second intervals)

The Bouncie plugs directly into your car's OBD-II port (the diagnostic port under the dashboard) and draws power from the vehicle — meaning no batteries to charge, ever. It provides real-time GPS tracking plus vehicle diagnostics: engine codes, battery voltage, coolant temperature, and driving behavior analysis.

For exotic car owners, the diagnostic features add a layer of value beyond tracking. You can monitor your car's health remotely — useful if it's in storage, at a service center, or being driven by someone else. The $8/month service fee is the lowest of any real-time tracker on the market.

The caveat: OBD-II trackers are visible and can be unplugged by a knowledgeable thief. For maximum security, pair a Bouncie with a hidden magnetic tracker like the LandAirSea Overdrive — belt and suspenders.

Best for: Daily-driven exotics where vehicle diagnostics and affordable monitoring are priorities.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. Spytec GL300 GPS Tracker — Best Covert Option

Price: ~$30 device + $17–25/month service | Battery: Up to 2.5 weeks (rechargeable) | Update Rate: Real-time (5-second intervals)

The Spytec GL300 is one of the smallest GPS trackers available — about the size of your thumb. It can be hidden virtually anywhere: inside a door panel, under a seat, in the trunk lining, or tucked into the engine bay. Its diminutive size makes it nearly impossible for a thief to find and disable, even if they're looking.

The trade-off is battery life — about 2.5 weeks on a single charge with frequent updates. You can extend this to several weeks by reducing update frequency to every 60 seconds, but for real-time theft recovery, you want the faster intervals.

Spytec's app is excellent, with geofencing, speed alerts, trip history, and SOS notification features. The monthly service is competitive at $17–25 depending on the plan.

Best for: Owners who want a truly hidden tracker that's nearly impossible to detect and disable.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. Apple AirTag (with Holder) — Best Supplemental Tracker

Price: ~$29 device + $0/month | Battery: ~1 year (CR2032) | Network: Apple Find My (crowd-sourced)

Let's be clear: an Apple AirTag is not a GPS tracker. It doesn't have GPS. It uses Apple's Find My network — the billion+ Apple devices in the world — to crowd-source its location. In a city like Miami, where iPhones are everywhere, this actually works remarkably well. Location updates come every few minutes as nearby Apple devices anonymously relay the AirTag's position.

The AirTag's strengths are its tiny size, zero monthly cost, and 1-year battery life. Hide one (or several) in your exotic's door panels, trunk, and interior, and you have a backup tracking layer that works independently of cellular-based trackers. If a thief finds and disables your primary tracker, the AirTags continue reporting.

The limitations: Location accuracy is lower (within a block vs. within a few feet for GPS). Updates are not real-time. And Apple's anti-stalking features will alert the thief's iPhone that an "unknown AirTag is traveling with you" after a period of time — though by then, law enforcement should already be notified.

Best for: A supplemental backup layer alongside a primary GPS tracker. At $29 with no monthly fee, there's no reason not to add a few to your exotic.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. CARLOCK Anti-Theft System — Best for Real-Time Driver Alerts

Price: ~$60 device + $10/month service | Battery: Vehicle-powered (OBD-II) | Update Rate: Real-time

CARLOCK is specifically designed as an anti-theft and driver monitoring system rather than a simple tracker. It plugs into your OBD-II port and provides real-time alerts for:

  • Engine start: Get a push notification the instant your car's engine starts — even if it's 3 AM.
  • Unusual vibration: Detects if your car is being towed or loaded onto a flatbed.
  • Device disconnection: Alerts you immediately if someone unplugs the tracker from the OBD-II port.
  • Unusual driving: Flags aggressive acceleration, hard braking, and driving patterns that don't match your profile — useful for valet monitoring.

The vibration detection is particularly valuable for Miami exotic owners. Flatbed theft — where a tow truck simply loads your car — is a growing method for stealing high-end vehicles because it bypasses steering locks and wheel boots entirely. CARLOCK detects the movement and alerts you before the truck pulls away.

Best for: Owners who want proactive theft prevention alerts, not just post-theft tracking.

Our Recommended Setup for Miami Exotic Owners

For maximum protection, we recommend a layered approach:

  1. Primary tracker: LandAirSea Overdrive hidden in a covert location (inside a bumper, under the dash, etc.) — real-time GPS with year-long battery life.
  2. Alert system: CARLOCK on the OBD-II port for instant engine start, tow, and disconnect alerts.
  3. Backup layer: 2–3 Apple AirTags hidden throughout the car as a secondary tracking network that works even if cellular trackers are jammed or disabled.

Total cost: roughly $150 in devices + $30/month in service. For a car worth $200K+, that's a rounding error compared to the peace of mind — and the dramatically improved odds of recovery if the worst happens.

Installation Tips for Exotic Cars

Where to Hide a GPS Tracker

The best hiding spots are areas a thief won't check in the critical first 30 minutes:

  • Inside the rear bumper: Most exotics have accessible space inside the rear bumper fascia. The LandAirSea Overdrive's magnetic mount attaches directly to any metal bracket.
  • Behind interior trim panels: Door cards, center console trim, and trunk lining panels can often be removed to tuck a tracker behind them.
  • Inside the spare tire well: If your exotic has one (many don't, but SUVs like the Urus do), it's a classic hiding spot.
  • Engine bay: In a waterproof enclosure, tucked away from heat sources. Less ideal due to extreme temperatures, but very difficult for thieves to access quickly.

Professional Installation

For hardwired trackers or complex installations, consider professional help. Several Miami shops specialize in covert vehicle security:

  • Most authorized exotic dealership service departments will install trackers during routine service
  • Mobile installation services can come to your home or office for discrete setup

Do GPS Trackers Lower Insurance Premiums?

Yes — potentially significantly. High-value vehicle insurers increasingly factor GPS tracking into their risk assessment:

  • Hagerty: May offer premium reductions for vehicles with documented tracking systems
  • Chubb Private Client: Actively considers vehicle security measures including GPS tracking in premium calculations
  • Pure Insurance: Has been known to require GPS tracking on vehicles above certain value thresholds

Ask your insurer specifically. Even a 5% premium reduction on a $12,000/year exotic car policy saves $600 annually — more than covering the cost of a GPS tracker subscription.

Legal Considerations in Florida

In Florida, it is legal to install a GPS tracker on a vehicle you own. If you're tracking a vehicle owned by someone else (even a spouse), the legality becomes murky — consult an attorney. For exotic car owners tracking their own vehicles, there are no legal barriers. Just don't forget to mention the tracker to your insurance company — the disclosure may help your rates.

Bottom Line

In Miami, the question isn't whether you need a GPS tracker on your exotic car — it's which one. The LandAirSea Overdrive is our top pick for most owners, offering the best combination of real-time tracking, battery life, and value. Layer it with Apple AirTags as backup and a CARLOCK for instant alerts, and you have a security system that gives you — and law enforcement — the best possible chance of recovering your investment.

A $30 tracker protecting a $300,000 car. The math speaks for itself. 📍

title: McLaren Senna: The Ultimate Track Hypercar You Can Own
excerpt: With just 500 units built, the McLaren Senna is one of the most extreme road-legal hypercars ever made. Here's everything you need to know about buying, owning, and driving one in Miami.
content:
The McLaren Senna is not a car you buy to cruise down Ocean Drive. Named after the greatest Formula 1 driver who ever lived, the Senna was designed with one singular purpose: to be the fastest McLaren around a racetrack while still wearing a license plate. With only 500 units ever produced and a current market hovering between $1.2 million and $2.5 million depending on spec and mileage, the McLaren Senna has cemented itself as one of the most collectible hypercars of the modern era.

McLaren Senna Specs and Performance

At the heart of the McLaren Senna sits a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 producing 789 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. That power routes through a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission to the rear wheels, launching the car from 0 to 60 mph in just 2.7 seconds and on to a top speed of 211 mph. But raw speed isn't the Senna's party trick — downforce is. The Senna generates up to 1,764 pounds of downforce at 155 mph, more than any road-legal McLaren before it. The massive rear wing, aggressive front splitter, and sculpted bodywork all serve aerodynamic function over aesthetic form.

Why the McLaren Senna Is Special

McLaren has built faster cars (the Speedtail) and more exclusive ones (the Sabre), but the Senna occupies a unique space in the lineup. It's the distillation of McLaren's racing DNA into a street-legal package with zero compromises. The carbon fiber monocoque chassis — called the Monocage III — weighs just 200 pounds and provides the structural foundation for the entire car. The body panels are all carbon fiber too, and McLaren even used carbon fiber for the roof scoop and engine bay cover. The dry weight of 2,641 pounds is absurdly light for a car this powerful.

The suspension is a double-wishbone setup front and rear with adaptive dampers linked to McLaren's RaceActive Chassis Control II system. In Track mode, the car lowers itself and stiffens to a degree that would be punishing on public roads — which is by design. The Senna wants to be on a track. It tolerates the road.

McLaren Senna Driving Experience

Reviews from professional drivers consistently describe the Senna as telepathic. The hydraulic steering provides feedback that most modern cars have engineered out. The brakes — carbon ceramic discs clamped by six-piston calipers up front and four-piston units at the rear — can haul the car from 124 mph to a dead stop in just 100 meters. Visibility is surprisingly good for a hypercar, thanks to the dihedral doors with their glass panels that McLaren calls "teardrop" windows, and the glass panels built into the lower door sections.

The interior strips away everything unnecessary. There's no infotainment touchscreen, no leather-wrapped dashboard, no luxury pretensions. The seats are carbon fiber shells with minimal padding. The door pulls are fabric straps. Climate control exists but is basic. Every gram saved from the interior went toward making the car faster on track. If you want comfort, buy a GT. The Senna is a weapon.

McLaren Senna Variants

Beyond the standard Senna, McLaren produced a few special variants worth knowing about:

  • McLaren Senna GTR: The track-only version. With 814 horsepower, a longer and wider body, and unrestricted aerodynamics, the GTR generates even more downforce and is significantly faster on circuit. Only 75 were made, and prices start around $3.5 million on the secondary market.
  • McLaren Senna LM: Just 20 units produced, created by McLaren Special Operations (MSO) to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the F1 GTR's 1995 Le Mans victory. Each was painted in one of five heritage liveries. These rarely trade hands, but when they do, they command north of $3 million.
  • McLaren Senna Can-Am: Another MSO special, limited to 20 cars, inspired by the legendary Can-Am racing series. Unique liveries and interior touches distinguish these from standard Sennas.

McLaren Senna for Sale: What to Know

If you're shopping for a McLaren Senna in the Miami area, here's the reality. Inventory is thin — at any given time, there might be five to ten available nationwide through dealers and private sellers. Miami-based dealers like The Collection in Coral Gables and Prestige Imports in North Miami Beach occasionally have Sennas in stock. Online platforms like DuPont Registry, Bring a Trailer, and Exotic Car Trader are the best places to monitor availability.

Owning a McLaren Senna in Miami

Miami is arguably the best city in America to own a hypercar. No state income tax, year-round driving weather, and a culture that celebrates automotive excess. But a few practical considerations apply to the Senna specifically:

  • Insurance: Expect to pay $15,000 to $30,000 annually for full coverage, depending on your driving record and agreed value.
  • Maintenance: Annual service costs run $3,000 to $5,000 for standard maintenance. Major services (every three years) can exceed $10,000. The carbon ceramic brakes cost over $20,000 to replace — but they last a long time with normal use.
  • Storage: The Senna sits very low (under 4 inches of front ground clearance), so driveways with steep angles are a problem. Many Miami owners keep theirs in climate-controlled garages at facilities like Curated in Wynwood or Gotham Dream Garage in the Design District.
  • Track access: Homestead-Miami Speedway and the soon-to-expand Palm Beach International Raceway give Senna owners nearby circuits to actually use the car as intended. Several track-day organizations run regular events at both venues.

McLaren Senna vs. the Competition

The Senna's direct rivals — the Ferrari FXX-K Evo (track only), Aston Martin Valkyrie, and Mercedes-AMG One — each take a different approach to the ultimate performance car. The Senna's advantage is its relative simplicity. No hybrid system, no electric motors, just a twin-turbo V8, lightweight construction, and insane aerodynamics. That simplicity translates to reliability and lower running costs compared to hybrid hypercars, and it makes the driving experience more visceral and connected.

Is the McLaren Senna a Good Investment?

The Senna has appreciated steadily since its original MSRP of approximately $959,000. Low-production McLarens with motorsport heritage tend to hold value well, and the Senna checks every box: named after a legend, limited to 500 cars, lauded by every journalist who drove it, and never likely to be repeated. Most automotive market analysts consider the Senna one of the safer blue-chip hypercars, though values can fluctuate with the broader collector car market.

For Miami collectors building a portfolio of significant cars, the Senna is a strong anchor alongside models like the Porsche 918 Spyder and Ferrari LaFerrari. It's not just a car — it's a piece of McLaren racing history made street legal.

title: Pininfarina Battista: Miami's Next Electric Hypercar
excerpt: The Pininfarina Battista is a 1,877-horsepower all-electric hypercar that perfectly fits Miami's luxury lifestyle. Here's the full breakdown on specs, pricing, and what it's like to own one in South Florida.
content:
The Pininfarina Battista is what happens when one of the most legendary design houses in automotive history decides to build the most powerful Italian car ever made — and make it fully electric. With 1,877 horsepower, a 0-60 time under two seconds, and a starting price of approximately \.2 million, the Battista is not just an electric hypercar. It's a statement about where the future of extreme performance is heading. And in Miami, where electric vehicle culture is booming alongside the city's love affair with exotic cars, the Battista fits right in.

Pininfarina Battista Performance Specs

The numbers are staggering. Four electric motors — one per wheel — produce a combined 1,877 horsepower and 1,696 lb-ft of torque. That makes the Battista more powerful than a Bugatti Chiron. The sprint from 0 to 60 mph takes less than 1.9 seconds, and the car reaches 186 mph in under 12 seconds. Top speed is electronically limited to 217 mph. The 120-kWh battery pack delivers an estimated range of approximately 300 miles on the WLTP cycle, though aggressive driving will significantly reduce that. Pininfarina Battista Design: Art on Wheels

Pininfarina has been designing cars since 1930 — shaping some of the most beautiful Ferraris, Maseratis, and Alfa Romeos in history. The Battista is their first car as a manufacturer, not just a design consultancy, and they poured nine decades of aesthetic mastery into it. The silhouette is dramatic but cohesive: flowing lines, a low-slung profile, and active aerodynamic elements that deploy based on speed and driving mode. The front features a signature Pininfarina curve that flows from the nose over the front fenders and down the body sides.

Inside, the cabin is handcrafted in Italy with materials that include sustainable leather alternatives, anodized aluminum, and carbon fiber. Every Battista is essentially bespoke — the company offers a personalization program called "Battista Bespoke" with virtually unlimited color and material combinations. The wraparound cockpit features a driver-focused layout with two digital screens — one for the instrument cluster and one for ancillary functions — plus a minimalist center console with rotary drive mode selectors.

Why the Pininfarina Battista Fits Miami

Miami's relationship with electric vehicles is evolving fast. Tesla dominates the roads, Lucid has a studio in Boca Raton, and Rimac — whose technology underpins the Battista — has been gaining recognition through collaborations with Porsche and Bugatti. The Battista slots into Miami's luxury scene as something genuinely different from the Ferraris and Lamborghinis that dominate the usual valet lines on South Beach.

  • Zero emissions, maximum presence: The Battista turns heads without making a sound. In a city that recently cracked down on loud exhaust in South Beach entertainment districts, an electric hypercar that still looks like a spaceship is a compelling proposition.
  • Charging infrastructure: Miami-Dade County has been expanding its EV charging network aggressively. Luxury condos in Brickell and Miami Beach are adding high-speed chargers to parking garages, and Electrify America stations along I-95 and the Turnpike provide DC fast charging for longer drives.
  • Climate advantage: Unlike cold-weather cities where EV range suffers in winter, Miami's warm climate is actually ideal for battery performance and range consistency year-round.
  • Car culture fit: Miami collectors already own cars from rare marques. Adding the first all-electric Italian hypercar to a collection that includes a Ferrari, Lamborghini, and Pagani makes a statement about forward-thinking taste.

Pininfarina Battista Pricing and Availability

Only 150 Battistas will ever be built, making it significantly rarer than the McLaren Senna (500 units) or even the Ferrari LaFerrari (499 units). Pricing starts at approximately \.2 million before personalization, which can add several hundred thousand dollars depending on spec. Deliveries to US customers began in late 2023 and are ongoing, with the production run expected to complete by 2026 or early 2027.

Pininfarina operates a direct sales model — there are no traditional dealerships. The company has brand experience spaces in key markets. In the US, the closest touchpoint for Miami buyers is through Pininfarina's North American operations. Several Miami-based exotic car dealers have listed pre-owned Battistas as well, though secondary market inventory remains extremely thin given the car's newness and limited production.

Pininfarina Battista vs. Rimac Nevera

The elephant in the room: the Rimac Nevera. Rimac supplies the core electric powertrain technology for the Battista, and the Nevera uses a similar quad-motor setup with 1,914 horsepower. They're related but distinct. The Nevera is a Croatian engineering showcase — raw, tech-forward, and brutally fast. The Battista is an Italian design statement built on that same technological foundation. Think of it this way: if the Nevera is a Formula 1 car, the Battista is the concours d'elegance entrant. Both are extraordinary. The Battista just wraps the performance in more emotional, sculptural bodywork. For Miami, where aesthetics matter as much as specs, that distinction is meaningful.

For Miami owners specifically, the Battista makes even more sense than it does in most markets. The warm climate optimizes battery performance, the charging infrastructure keeps improving, the quiet operation sidesteps noise enforcement, and the sheer visual drama of the car ensures it stands out even in a city drowning in Lamborghinis.   • Worst time to buy (November-March): Peak season. Northern buyers fly in, Art Basel drives December demand, and the Miami Grand Prix in May creates a spring surge. Markups are highest during these months.
  • End of quarter: Like any car dealer, Lamborghini dealers have quarterly targets. Late March, June, September, and December can yield better negotiating leverage on in-stock inventory.

Financing a Lamborghini in Miami

Most Lamborghini buyers in Miami finance their purchase, even when they could pay cash. Here's the landscape:

Miami is objectively one of the best places in America to own a Lamborghini. No state income tax means more money for the car. Year-round warm weather means year-round driving. The car culture embraces exotics rather than judging them. And the resale market is liquid — when you're ready to sell, there's always a buyer in South Florida.

The main risks are overpaying (especially during peak season or on markup-heavy new models), buying a former rental without knowing it, and underestimating ownership costs. Do your homework on the specific car, get a pre-purchase inspection from an independent Lamborghini specialist, and time your purchase for maximum leverage. A well-bought Lamborghini in Miami isn't just a car — it's a lifestyle asset that holds value better than most luxury purchases.

title: Best Premium Car Covers for Exotic Cars: Protect Your Miami Investment
excerpt: Miami's brutal sun, salt air, and hurricane season make a premium car cover essential for any garaged or outdoor exotic. Here are the best car covers for Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and more in 2026.
content:
Your exotic car's paint doesn't just face threats on the road — it faces them standing still. In Miami, a parked car battles UV radiation strong enough to fade paint in months, salt-laden coastal air that corrodes trim and brightwork, afternoon thunderstorms that leave mineral-heavy water spots, and the occasional hurricane that turns debris into projectiles. A premium car cover is the simplest, most cost-effective way to protect a six- or seven-figure investment when it's not being driven.

We've evaluated the best car covers for exotic cars based on what matters in South Florida: UV protection, breathability (critical in Miami's humidity), water resistance, soft inner linings that won't scratch delicate paint, and custom-fit options for specific exotic models.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need a Premium Car Cover

Even if your exotic lives in a garage, a cover is essential in Miami. Here's why:

  • UV damage through windows: Many Miami garages have windows or open sides. UV radiation penetrates and degrades paint, rubber seals, and interior materials even in covered parking. A quality cover blocks 99%+ of UV.
  • Dust and debris: Construction dust, concrete dust from parking structures, and general airborne particulate settle on your paint daily. Each speck is an abrasive waiting to scratch when something brushes against it.
  • Humidity and condensation: Miami's 70-80% average humidity means condensation forms on cool surfaces overnight. A breathable cover prevents moisture from pooling on paint while allowing trapped humidity to escape — preventing mold and mildew.
  • Hurricane prep: During hurricane season (June-November), a heavy-duty outdoor cover provides a last line of defense against wind-blown debris when you can't move the car to a hardened structure.
  • Valet and parking protection: A covered car signals "don't touch" to valets, parking attendants, and curious passersby. It's a psychological deterrent as much as a physical one.

Best Car Covers for Exotic Cars in 2026

Covercraft is the gold standard in custom car covers, and the WeatherShield HP is their premium all-weather option. Each cover is cut to the exact dimensions of your specific vehicle — not a generic "fits most sports cars" shape, but a pattern made for a 2024 Ferrari 296 GTB or a 2025 Lamborghini Revuelto specifically. The WeatherShield HP fabric is a single-layer woven material that's remarkably light yet blocks rain, UV, and dust. Why it's #1 for Miami: The combination of UV blocking, breathability, and water resistance is perfectly suited to South Florida's weather. Custom fit means it protects every contour of your exotic without bunching or flapping in wind.

Like Covercraft, Coverking offers custom patterns for specific vehicles. The inner lining is a soft fleece that protects paint from abrasion. It's water-resistant (not waterproof — important distinction for breathability) and includes reinforced grommets for tie-down straps in windy conditions.

Car Cover Sizing: Why Custom Fit Matters for Exotics

Generic "one size fits all" car covers are the automotive equivalent of wearing someone else's suit. On an exotic car, they're actively harmful:

  • Flapping in wind: A loose cover acts like sandpaper in a breeze, rubbing back and forth across paint with every gust. Miami's afternoon winds and storm gusts can cause real damage to clear coat under a loose cover.
  • Contact pressure: Covers that bunch up over spoilers, mirrors, or air intakes create pressure points. On a ceramic-coated or PPF-wrapped exotic, those pressure points can leave marks.
  • Water pooling: A poorly fitted cover creates pockets where water collects instead of running off. Pooled water + Florida sun = baked-on water spots under the cover.

Custom-fit covers follow every contour — the Urus's roofline, the Huracán's side scoops, the 911 Turbo's whale tail. The fit prevents all three issues and looks professional in a way that signals care to anyone who sees your car.

How to Use a Car Cover Without Scratching Your Exotic

A dirty cover on clean paint defeats the purpose. Follow these rules:

  1. Always cover a clean car: Any dirt on the paint surface will get ground in under the cover. Quick rinse or detail spray wipe before covering.
  2. Keep the cover clean: Machine wash your cover every 3-4 months (most premium covers are machine washable on gentle cycle). In Miami's dusty, pollen-heavy environment, a dirty cover is worse than no cover.
  3. Fold carefully: When removing, fold the cover soft-side-in to prevent the outer surface from touching paint. Never ball it up and toss it in the trunk.
  4. Dry before storing: If the cover is wet from rain, let it dry completely before storing it in its bag. A damp cover in a sealed bag = mildew, especially in Miami's humidity.

Hurricane Season Cover Strategy

During hurricane season (June through November), Miami exotic car owners need a plan. A car cover is one layer of protection, but it's not a substitute for proper storm preparation:

  • If you can evacuate the car: Drive it to a hardened indoor garage away from flood zones. Many Miami storage facilities offer hurricane-rated units — Gotham Dream Garage and similar facilities are built to withstand Category 3+ winds.
  • If the car stays: Use the heaviest-duty cover available (Platinum Shield or equivalent), secure it with tie-down straps, and park in the most protected area of your garage — away from windows and garage doors. Consider wrapping the car in moving blankets under the cover for added debris protection.
  • Post-storm: Remove the cover carefully after the storm. Debris, leaves, and standing water may be on top. Rinse the car thoroughly before any contact wash to remove abrasive particles.

Should You Use a Cover on a Ceramic-Coated or PPF-Wrapped Car?

Absolutely — but with caveats. Ceramic coatings and paint protection film (PPF) protect against chemical and minor physical damage, but they don't block UV degradation of the coating itself. A car cover extends the life of your ceramic coating by reducing UV exposure when the car is parked. Similarly, PPF can yellow over time with UV exposure; a cover slows that process significantly.

The key: use a cover with a soft inner lining (all five options above qualify). Rough inner surfaces can micro-scratch ceramic coatings, which defeats the purpose. The California Car Cover Multiweave 2 and Covercraft WeatherShield HP are particularly gentle on coated surfaces.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the Covercraft WeatherShield HP is the move — it handles everything Miami throws at it while being gentle enough for the most precious paint. If your car lives outdoors, the Coverking Silverguard Plus adds reflective UV protection that's invaluable under the South Florida sun. And for garage queens, the California Car Cover Multiweave 2 provides the softest, most breathable protection available.

A $350 cover protecting a $300,000 paint job. The math is simple. Cover your exotic. 🛡️
