title: Best Polishing Machines & Kits for Exotic Cars: A Miami Detailing Guide
excerpt: Miami's sun and salt air punish your exotic's paint. A quality polishing machine is how you fight back — removing swirls, restoring gloss, and prepping for ceramic coating. Here are the best polishers for 2026.
content:
Every exotic car in Miami has a secret: under the showroom shine, the paint is taking a beating. UV radiation oxidizes clear coat. Salt air etches microscopic pits. Automatic car washes (the ones you should never use on an exotic) leave swirl marks. Even hand washing with the wrong technique creates fine scratches visible under direct sunlight. The fix? A polishing machine — the single most transformative tool in any detailer's arsenal.

Machine polishing removes those imperfections by leveling the clear coat surface, restoring depth, gloss, and that "wet look" that makes a Ferrari look like it just rolled off the factory floor. It's also the essential prep step before applying ceramic coating — because coating locks in whatever's underneath, good or bad. We've tested and researched the best polishing machines and kits for exotic cars in 2026, with a focus on what works for Miami's unique conditions.

Why Machine Polishing Matters in Miami

Hand polishing is fine for a quick glaze, but it can't correct paint. Only a machine polisher generates the consistent speed, pressure, and heat needed to actually level clear coat imperfections. Here's why Miami exotic owners specifically need one:

  • UV oxidation: Miami's extreme UV index causes clear coat to oxidize faster than almost anywhere in the US. A polishing machine removes the dull, oxidized layer and reveals the fresh, glossy paint underneath.
  • Swirl mark removal: Even careful hand washing creates micro-swirls over time. On dark-colored exotics (Nero Daytona, Obsidian Black, Dark Blue Metallic), these swirls are painfully visible in Miami's intense sunlight. A DA polisher eliminates them.
  • Water spot etching: Miami's hard water and mineral-rich rain leave spots that can etch into clear coat if left untreated. Light machine polishing removes the etching without damaging the surrounding paint.
  • Ceramic coating prep: If you've read our ceramic coating guide, you know that paint correction before coating is mandatory. A polishing machine is how you do that correction.

Dual Action vs. Rotary: Which Polisher for Exotic Cars?

Before we get to specific products, you need to understand the two types of machine polishers:

Dual Action (DA) Polisher — Recommended for Most Owners

A DA polisher oscillates and rotates simultaneously, creating a random orbital pattern that's virtually impossible to burn through paint with. Even if you hold it in one spot too long, the dual action prevents heat buildup that could damage clear coat. This makes it the safe choice for exotic car owners who aren't professional detailers.

Rotary Polisher — For Experienced Users Only

A rotary spins the pad in a single direction, generating more cutting power and heat. In professional hands, a rotary can remove deep scratches and heavy oxidation faster than a DA. In inexperienced hands, it can burn through clear coat in seconds — a $5,000-$15,000 mistake on an exotic with multi-stage factory paint. Unless you have significant polishing experience, stick with a DA.

1. Rupes LHR21 Mark III BigFoot — Best Overall for Exotics

The Rupes BigFoot LHR21 is the polisher that professional detailers reach for when working on Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and Rolls-Royces — and there's a reason it's the industry standard. The 21mm orbit throws more correction per pass than smaller-orbit machines, meaning you spend less time polishing and reduce the risk of over-working the paint. The electronic speed control maintains consistent RPM under load, so the polisher doesn't bog down mid-panel.

The ergonomics are outstanding. At approximately 5.5 lbs, it's light enough for extended use without fatigue — important when you're spending 4-6 hours correcting an entire exotic. The backing plate and pad system is Rupes' proprietary design, optimized for their BigFoot pads, which are widely available and come in every cutting grade from heavy correction to ultra-fine finishing.

Why it's #1 for Miami: The 21mm orbit is aggressive enough to remove UV oxidation and water spot etching — the two most common paint issues in South Florida — while being safe enough that you won't burn through on your first attempt. Pro detailers in Miami overwhelmingly recommend this machine.

The Griot's G9 has a cult following in the detailing community, and for good reason. It delivers 80-90% of the Rupes' correction capability at roughly one-third the price. The 6-inch random orbital motion is safe on all paint types, the variable speed dial (2,000-6,800 OPM) gives you precise control, and the 25-foot power cord means you can work around an entire car without an extension cord.

What sets the G9 apart from similarly priced competitors is build quality. The motor is smooth, the bearings are robust, and the vibration is minimal — your hands won't go numb after an hour of use. Griot's also offers a lifetime warranty, which no other polisher in this price range matches.

The kit typically includes the TORQ 22D polisher, a set of hex-logic pads in multiple cutting grades (heavy, medium, finishing), V-Line compound and polish, microfiber towels, and a pad conditioner. The LHR15 is the smaller sibling of the LHR21, using a 15mm orbit and a 5-inch backing plate instead of 6 inches. Essential Compounds and Polishes for Miami Paint Issues

The polisher is the tool; the compound is what does the actual cutting. Here's what works best for South Florida's typical paint problems:

For UV Oxidation and Heavy Swirls

Meguiar's M110 Ultra Cut Compound (~$25) — The industry-standard heavy cutting compound. Removes oxidation, deep swirls, and water spot etching in one or two passes. Diminishing abrasive technology means it starts aggressive and finishes smooth, reducing the need for a follow-up polish on lighter defects.

For Light Swirls and Finishing

Meguiar's M210 Ultra Finishing Polish (~$25) — The companion to M110. After heavy correction, M210 removes the hazing left by the compound and brings the paint to a mirror-like finish. On light-colored exotics with only minor swirls, you can often skip M110 and go straight to M210.

For One-Step Correction

Sonax Perfect Finish 04-06 (~$30) — The one-step wonder. Sonax Perfect Finish cuts like a medium compound and finishes like a fine polish, making it possible to do a complete paint correction in a single step on all but the most damaged paint. It's the secret weapon of detailers who need efficiency without sacrificing results.

How to Machine Polish an Exotic Car: Step by Step

Before You Start

  1. Wash thoroughly: Use a foam cannon and two-bucket method (see our pressure washer guide). Any dirt left on the surface will cause scratching during polishing.
  2. Clay bar: After washing, use a clay bar or clay mitt to remove embedded contaminants — iron particles, tree sap, overspray. The surface should feel glass-smooth before polishing.
  3. Tape off trim: Use painter's tape to protect rubber seals, plastic trim, and badges. Compound residue is difficult to remove from textured surfaces.

The Polishing Process

  1. Apply compound: 3-4 pea-sized drops on the pad. Spread at low speed (speed 1-2) across a 2ft × 2ft section before increasing speed.
  2. Work the section: Increase to speed 4-5. Use overlapping passes (50% overlap) in a crosshatch pattern — horizontal passes, then vertical. Moderate, consistent pressure. Let the machine do the work.
  3. Work until the compound breaks down: You'll see the compound go from opaque to nearly transparent. That's when the diminishing abrasives have finished their job.
  4. Wipe and inspect: Remove residue with a clean microfiber towel. Inspect under a bright LED light (or direct sunlight) at multiple angles. If swirls remain, repeat with the same pad and compound, or step up to a heavier-cutting pad.
  5. Follow with finishing polish: Switch to a finishing pad and fine polish (M210 or equivalent) for maximum gloss.
  6. Final wipe: Use an IPA (isopropyl alcohol) wipe or panel prep spray to remove all oils. This reveals the true correction results and preps the surface for ceramic coating or sealant.

Miami-Specific Polishing Tips

  • Work in shade or garage: Never polish in direct Miami sunlight. The compound dries too fast, creates a haze that's hard to remove, and the polisher can overheat. A climate-controlled garage between 65-80°F is ideal.
  • Morning sessions: If you're working in a non-air-conditioned garage, start early. By noon in Miami's summer, garage temperatures can exceed 100°F — too hot for comfortable polishing and for the compounds to perform optimally.
  • Stay hydrated: This sounds obvious, but polishing an entire exotic car takes 4-8 hours. In Miami heat, dehydration sneaks up fast. Keep water nearby.
  • Don't skip the clay bar: Miami's environment deposits more contaminants on paint than most places — sea salt, iron particles from construction, industrial fallout from the port. Skipping the clay bar step means polishing those contaminants into the paint, causing more damage than you're fixing.

How Often Should You Polish an Exotic in Miami?

Full paint correction (heavy compound + finishing polish) should be done once or twice a year at most. Each polishing session removes a thin layer of clear coat — necessary to eliminate defects, but you don't want to do it excessively. Most factory exotic clear coats are 2-4 mils thick; each polishing pass removes about 0.1-0.5 mils depending on the compound and pad.

Between full corrections, maintain the finish with:

  • Ceramic coating: Applied after correction, lasts 2-5 years, protects the freshly polished surface
  • Spray sealant: Quick monthly application that adds a protective layer over the coating
  • Proper washing: Foam cannon + two-bucket method to avoid reintroducing swirls

If your exotic is ceramic coated and properly washed, you may only need a full machine polish every 18-24 months — even in Miami's harsh conditions.

Professional Polishing vs. DIY in Miami

Professional paint correction on an exotic car in Miami typically runs $500-$1,500 for a one-step polish, or $800-$2,500 for a full multi-stage correction. That's real money, but you're paying for experience, lighting rigs that reveal defects, and the confidence that comes from having corrected hundreds of six-figure paint jobs.

DIY with a Griot's G9 or Chemical Guys TORQ Kit at $130-$250 gets you started for the cost of one professional session. The learning curve is real — expect your first car to take twice as long as an experienced detailer's — but dual-action polishers are forgiving enough that you won't cause damage while learning.

Our recommendation: If you've never polished a car before, start on a less precious vehicle (your daily driver, a family member's car) before touching your exotic. Once you're comfortable with pad selection, compound amounts, and speed settings, you'll have the confidence to tackle your Ferrari or Lamborghini.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the Griot's Garage G9 delivers outstanding results at an accessible price — pair it with Meguiar's M110 and M210 for a correction system that handles UV oxidation, swirl marks, and water spot etching. If you want the tool that Miami's best professional detailers actually use on million-dollar cars, the Rupes LHR21 Mark III is the investment piece that will serve you for decades. And if you want to start with everything in one box, the Chemical Guys TORQ 22D Kit takes the guesswork out of your first paint correction.

In Miami, polishing isn't cosmetic — it's maintenance. Your exotic's paint is under constant assault from the sun, salt, and elements. A quality polishing machine is how you fight back. ✨

title: Aston Martin for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Dealers & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: Looking for an Aston Martin for sale in Miami? Here's every model, current pricing, and which dealers carry them — from brand-new Vantages to pre-owned DB11s.
content:
If you're searching for an Aston Martin for sale in Miami, you're in one of the best cities in the country to find one. South Florida has one of the highest concentrations of luxury and exotic car dealerships in the United States, and Aston Martin has a strong presence here. Whether you want a brand-new 2026 Vantage, a certified pre-owned DB11, or a collector-grade DBS Superleggera, Miami's market has options that most cities simply don't.

This guide covers current Aston Martin pricing for every model available in 2026, the best dealerships in Miami to buy from, and what you need to know before writing that check.

Aston Martin Models & Pricing in Miami (2026)

Aston Martin's current lineup spans grand tourers, sports cars, SUVs, and limited-production hypercars. Here's what each model costs and what you can expect to find on Miami dealer lots right now.

Miami Aston Martin prices typically run 3-8% above MSRP on new models due to South Florida's strong demand and limited allocations. Pre-owned models can actually be better deals here because the supply of trade-ins is higher than in most markets — Miami buyers cycle through cars fast.

Best Aston Martin Dealers in Miami

Aston Martin Miami (The Collection)

The Collection in Coral Gables is the official Aston Martin dealer for the greater Miami area and one of the top-performing Aston Martin dealerships in North America. Located at 200 Bird Road, their showroom typically has 20-30 new Aston Martins in stock at any given time, plus a strong selection of certified pre-owned vehicles. If you're buying new and want allocation priority on limited models like the Valhalla, this is where your relationship needs to be. Their service department is factory-certified, which matters when you're dealing with a car that has a hand-built V12.

Prestige Imports

While primarily a Lamborghini dealer, Prestige Imports on South Dixie Highway frequently has pre-owned Aston Martins in their inventory. They're worth checking for DB11s, Vantages, and the occasional DBS that came in on trade. Their pricing on pre-owned Aston Martins tends to be competitive because they're not an Aston franchise and don't carry the brand premium.

Warren Henry Auto Group

Warren Henry in North Miami handles multiple luxury brands and often stocks pre-owned Aston Martins. They've been in the Miami luxury car business for decades and have a solid reputation for straight dealing. Good option if you want to compare an Aston Martin against a Bentley or Range Rover at the same location.

Private Sellers & Consignment

Curated Miami on NW 2nd Avenue specializes in consignment sales of high-end exotics and frequently lists Aston Martins. Bring a Buyer from DuPont Registry is another avenue — many Miami Aston Martin owners list their cars on DuPont before going to a dealer. For pre-owned purchases, always get a pre-purchase inspection (PPI) from an independent Aston Martin specialist before committing.

New vs. Pre-Owned Aston Martin: What Makes Sense in Miami

Aston Martins depreciate significantly in the first 2-3 years. A DB11 that stickered for 20,000 new can often be found pre-owned with under 15,000 miles for 30,000-50,000. That's a massive savings, and the car is still essentially new. Miami's pre-owned market is particularly strong because owners here tend to keep cars in excellent cosmetic condition — garage-kept, detailed regularly, no salt road damage (Florida doesn't salt roads).

The exception is limited-production models. The Valkyrie, Valhalla, and any special-edition DBS will hold value or appreciate. If you can get an allocation on one of these, take it — they're investments as much as they are cars.

Aston Martin Price Trends to Watch in 2026

Several factors are affecting Aston Martin prices in the Miami market right now:

  • DB12 launch effect: The DB12 replaced the DB11, pushing DB11 pre-owned prices down 10-15%. Great time to buy a used DB11.
  • DBX707 demand: The super-SUV segment is white-hot in Miami. DBX707s are selling at or above MSRP with minimal time on lots.
  • Valhalla hype: With deliveries starting in late 2026, allocation holders are already fielding offers above sticker. If you didn't get on the list early, expect to pay a premium on the secondary market.
  • Classic Aston Martins: Vintage DB5s, DB6s, and V8 Vantages from the 1980s continue to climb. Miami's car show circuit has driven demand for these significantly.

Financing an Aston Martin in Miami

Most Miami Aston Martin buyers finance, even when they don't need to. With rates in the current market, many buyers prefer to keep capital invested rather than tying it up in a depreciating asset. The Collection offers in-house financing through Aston Martin Financial Services, typically at 5.9-7.9% APR depending on credit and term. For better rates, check with:

  • Woodside Credit: Specializes in exotic car loans, often has the best rates for high-value vehicles
  • LightStream: Unsecured personal loans up to 00K with competitive rates for excellent credit
  • PNC Premier Banking: Strong presence in South Florida with dedicated exotic car lending

Leasing is another popular option — see our complete Aston Martin lease guide for Miami for current lease deals and terms.

What to Inspect Before Buying a Pre-Owned Aston Martin

Aston Martins are hand-built and beautifully engineered, but they have maintenance needs that differ from mass-market cars. Before buying pre-owned, make sure you check:

  • Service history: Aston Martin service intervals are strict. Missed services can void remaining warranty and signal neglect.
  • Transmission: The automated manual (Sportshift) in older models is a known weak point. Test for smooth shifting and listen for grinding or hesitation.
  • Cooling system: In Miami's heat, cooling system components work overtime. Check for leaks, coolant condition, and fan operation.
  • Paint and clear coat: Florida sun damages clear coat. Inspect for fading, orange peel, and whether the car has been ceramic coated (a good sign).
  • Interior leather: Heat and UV destroy leather. Check for cracking on the dash, door cards, and seats.

Total annual cost of ownership ranges from roughly 2,000 to 5,000 depending on the model and how you use it. Factor this in when budgeting — the purchase price is just the beginning.

Where to Find the Best Aston Martin Deals in Miami

The best time to buy an Aston Martin in Miami is typically late summer through early fall. Dealers are clearing inventory before new model year allocations arrive, and you'll find the most aggressive pricing on outgoing models. End-of-quarter (March, June, September, December) also produces deals as dealerships push to hit volume targets. For pre-owned, keep an eye on Curated Miami, DuPont Registry, and Bring a Trailer — some of the best deals on pre-owned Aston Martins come through consignment and auction rather than traditional dealerships.

title: Aston Martin Valhalla: Specs, Price & What Miami Buyers Need to Know
excerpt: The Aston Martin Valhalla is the brand's first hybrid supercar — a 998-hp mid-engine monster arriving in late 2026. Here's everything about specs, pricing, and getting one in Miami.
content:
The Aston Martin Valhalla is the most important car Aston Martin has built in decades. It's the brand's first mid-engine production car, its first plug-in hybrid, and the bridge between Aston Martin's grand touring heritage and a future defined by electrification and extreme performance. With a combined output of 998 horsepower from a twin-turbo V8 and three electric motors, the Valhalla isn't just an evolution — it's a statement that Aston Martin can compete with Ferrari, McLaren, and Porsche at the absolute top of the supercar pyramid.

For Miami buyers who've been following the Valhalla's development since its debut as the AM-RB 003 concept, the wait is almost over. Production is ramping up at Aston Martin's Gaydon facility with deliveries expected to begin in late 2026. Here's everything you need to know.

Aston Martin Valhalla Specifications

Aston Martin Valhalla Price

The Aston Martin Valhalla has a base price of approximately 00,000. However, "base price" is a loose term for a car like this — virtually every Valhalla will be optioned significantly. Aston Martin's Q by Aston Martin personalization program allows buyers to specify bespoke paint colors, interior materials, carbon fiber finishes, and unique design touches that can push the final price well above 00,000.

On the secondary market, expect premiums. With only 999 units being produced and allocations already spoken for at most dealerships worldwide, any Valhalla that hits the resale market before 2028 will likely trade above million. This is following the same pattern we saw with the Ferrari SF90 Stradale, McLaren Speedtail, and Porsche 918 Spyder — limited-run hybrid supercars appreciate immediately when demand exceeds production.

How the Valhalla Compares to Its Rivals

The Valhalla enters a rarefied segment of hybrid supercars. Here's how it stacks up against the competition you'll see parked on Ocean Drive:

Ferrari SF90 XX Stradale1,016 hp2.3s50,000+Limited

Porsche 918 Spyder (used)887 hp2.5s,800,000+918 units

The Valhalla occupies a compelling position: more affordable than the McLaren W1 and AMG ONE, similar power to the Ferrari SF90 XX, and dramatically more exclusive than anything at this price point. For Miami collectors who want a hybrid hypercar without committing million or more, the Valhalla is arguably the smartest play.

Design & Aerodynamics

The Valhalla's design is defined by its aerodynamic function. Every surface, vent, and curve serves a purpose — Aston Martin claims 600 kg of downforce at 150 mph, which puts it in genuine race-car territory. Key design elements include:

  • Active aerodynamics: A rear wing that adjusts angle and height based on speed and driving mode, plus underbody venturi tunnels for ground effect downforce
  • Top-exit exhaust: The exhaust exits through the rear bodywork above the diffuser, keeping underbody airflow clean — a solution borrowed from F1 engineering
  • Dihedral doors: The signature butterfly-style doors hinge forward and upward, making the Valhalla unmistakable in Miami traffic or at a valet stand
  • Carbon fiber monocoque: The entire tub is carbon fiber, keeping weight down despite the hybrid system's battery pack

In terms of visual presence, the Valhalla is lower, wider, and more aggressive than any road-going Aston Martin before it. It looks like nothing else in the lineup — this isn't a GT with hybrid power bolted on. It's a purpose-built supercar that happens to wear an Aston Martin badge.

The Hybrid System Explained

The Valhalla's powertrain is genuinely innovative. The 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 sits behind the cockpit and drives the rear wheels through an 8-speed DCT. Two electric motors on the front axle provide instant torque and all-wheel-drive capability, while a third motor integrated into the transmission fills in torque gaps during gear changes — eliminating the momentary power dip you feel in conventional dual-clutch gearboxes.

The electric-only range of approximately 9 miles might seem modest, but it's enough for short city hops — like driving from your Brickell condo to Komodo without firing up the V8. When you want full performance, all three motors and the V8 work together to deliver that 998 horsepower figure. The system also enables torque vectoring on the front axle, which makes the Valhalla remarkably agile for a car with this much power.

Getting a Valhalla in Miami

If you want an Aston Martin Valhalla in Miami, your primary path is through The Collection (Aston Martin Miami) in Coral Gables. As the authorized Aston Martin dealer for the greater Miami area, they handle all new-car allocations. However, with only 999 units being built globally, securing an allocation is highly competitive.

Here's the reality of getting one:

  • Existing clients first: Aston Martin prioritizes buyers with a purchase history. If you've previously bought an Aston Martin through The Collection, you're in a stronger position.
  • Deposit required: Expect a substantial deposit (typically 0,000-00,000) to hold a production slot, refundable if you back out before spec lock.
  • Spec your car early: Q by Aston Martin personalization takes time. Early allocation holders can spend months choosing colors, materials, and options.
  • Secondary market: If allocations are sold out, your other option is buying a delivery slot from another buyer or purchasing a completed car on the secondary market. Expect a significant premium — potentially 00,000 or more above sticker.

Why the Valhalla Matters for Miami Car Culture

Miami's exotic car scene has historically been dominated by Italian and German brands — Lamborghini, Ferrari, Porsche, and McLaren own the streets. Aston Martin has always had a presence, but more in the grand touring space than the hardcore supercar segment. The Valhalla changes that equation entirely.

A 998-hp hybrid supercar with butterfly doors and a sub-3-second 0-60 time competes head-to-head with anything parked on Ocean Drive. And frankly, it'll stand out more than another Huracán or 911 Turbo S — Miami has thousands of those. A Valhalla? There might be a handful in all of South Florida.

For collectors and enthusiasts, the Valhalla also represents a smart investment. Limited-production hybrid hypercars from this era — the transitional period between pure ICE and full electric — are likely to be highly collectible. The Porsche 918 Spyder, which launched at 45,000, now trades for nearly double that. The Valhalla could follow a similar trajectory.

Aston Martin Valhalla: The Bottom Line

The Aston Martin Valhalla delivers 998 horsepower, a carbon fiber monocoque, hybrid AWD, dihedral doors, and genuine supercar performance for 00,000 — making it one of the most compelling limited-production hypercars on the market. For Miami buyers with the means and the foresight to secure an allocation, it's a car that will define the next chapter of Aston Martin's story and hold serious value for years to come.

If you're serious about getting one, start the conversation with your dealer now. With 999 units worldwide, hesitation is the only thing that guarantees you miss out.
